rationale:
Evidence: the iteration 8 design (sensor span x = ±0.05, kd 0.6, sensor_size 0.012, base_speed 1.5, kp 4.0, ki 0.2, weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), last_direction) raced at 323.64 in iteration 8 and reproduced exactly in iteration 9. That confirms the baseline. Oval finishes are 14 of 20 and mean oval progress is 0.93. Line losses are 0.75 on the s-bend and 1.00 on the slalom, and every s-bend and slalom run still ends off track. Oval steering_oscillation is 0.40, above the 0.32 threshold set in earlier reviews. Earlier span and sensor tests have already been run: ±0.06 cut finishes (219.9), sensor_size 0.016 dropped the score to 157.9, and base_speed 1.3 dropped it to 86.8. Those levers stay closed.

Change: kd 0.6 to 0.55, with the span held at ±0.05 and every other value unchanged. This is the single-variable test the Evaluator's branch rule called for, since the score held near 323 and finishes stayed at 14 of 20. The kd gain at span 0.04 was positive (kd 0.55 to 0.6 gave +44), so there is a real risk that kd 0.55 gives a lower score. The reason to test it anyway is that oval oscillation (0.40) is the one warning sign, and it is the clearest open question about damping at this span. If kd 0.55 scores below 323.64, the next iteration should revert to kd 0.6 at span 0.05, which is the proven design.

Expected result: score near 323 to 335, with oval oscillation below 0.40 and finishes at 13 to 14 of 20. Hypotheses: (a) kd 0.6 is slightly too high at span 0.05 and causes the oval oscillation; (b) kd 0.55 keeps the finish gains, so the score is roughly unchanged. Measurements wanted: per-track line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, plus oval completion and completion_time, so the damping effect can be separated from the span effect.
